judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences; 'unless otherwise indicated' is a soft qualifier but each Extension states its own status.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies Coinsurance (c065) to the Extensions and makes them additional insurance, which must be squared with Limits Of Insurance (c053); the two can be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare cross-reference sentence with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Special Form (c099) is in fact attached, so the reference resolves cleanly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The most we will pay for loss or damage in any one occurrence is the applicable Limit of Insurance shown in the Declarations' is compact, but 'applicable' does real work where several limits could apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations write blanket Building, Contents and Business Income limits over nine locations while other provisions (c042, c051, c065) treat limits building-by-building, which is a genuine whole-instrument tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but arithmetically specified with two worked examples; the order of operations is spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'separate Limits of Insurance' assumption sits awkwardly with the blanket limits in the Declarations and with Coinsurance (c065), which is applied first.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An applicability sentence with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It stacks the Loss Conditions on the Common and Commercial Property Conditions without displacing either.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single categorical sentence; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Loss Payment's option to take property at an agreed value (c059).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The OCR has dropped 'Pay its chosen appraiser' from the cost-sharing list, and 'competent and impartial' plus 'value of the property or the amount of loss' are the usual flashpoints.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 F (c195) replaces this condition with a voluntary appraisal that happens only if both parties agree, flatly contradicting the unilateral 'either may make written demand' printed here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard duties list studded with elastic phrases ('as soon as possible', 'all reasonable steps', 'as often as may be reasonably required') that a court can be asked to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the Business Income duties (c166) and is a precondition to suit under Legal Action Against Us (c021/c187); no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At our option' among four settlement methods, and 'other property of like kind and quality', are open-ended in a way that determines what the insured is paid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its flat statement that repair cost excludes ordinance-enforcement increases contradicts the Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage (c042), which says the Loss Payment limitation does not apply to its own payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At your option' with a clear repayment mechanic; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Transfer of Rights of Recovery (c026) and Loss Payment (c059).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The vacancy definition turns on '31% of its total square footage' being 'used ... to conduct customary operations', which for an apartment complex is a genuinely contestable measure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Building means the entire building' has to be applied to a nine-location blanket schedule (Declarations, c053), and c062 keys the 15% reduction to 'the building where loss or damage occurs'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of six causes plus a flat 15% reduction; the arithmetic is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends wholly on the vacancy definition in c061, whose 'building' meaning is uncertain across a blanket multi-building schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Actual cash value is left undefined here, the $2,500 repair rule is conditioned on satisfying Coinsurance, and the ordinance-cost sentence is a further qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Replacement Cost Optional Coverage replaces Actual Cash Value in this Valuation Condition and c188 supplies a Kansas ACV definition, while c042 removes the ordinance-cost limitation for code upgrades, so three provisions pull at this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An applicability sentence only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It layers Coinsurance and Mortgageholders onto the Common Policy Conditions without displacing them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The formula depends on 'the value of Covered Property at the time of loss', a basis the clause never fixes (ACV or replacement cost), and the printed Step (2) is truncated mid-sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 100% coinsurance shown in the Declarations must be applied to blanket limits covering nine buildings, while c051, c162 and the Agreed Value option disapply coinsurance in places and c042 uses the coinsurance percentage in a different formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The printed text is interleaved with unrelated Agreed Value and Inflation Guard paragraphs, so the mortgageholder rights run into a foreign example and lose their sequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.4 (c192) replaces paragraph b. for townhouse risks, giving two competing versions of who is paid.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence excluding 'the increased cost attributable to enforcement of any ordinance or law', a phrase whose reach over code-driven rebuilding costs is precisely what parties fight about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts the Increased Cost Of Construction Additional Coverage (c042), which applies only where Replacement Cost applies and expressly overrides the ordinance-cost limitations of the Loss Payment, Valuation and Replacement Cost provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditioned on a written contract governing liability with a 'lesser of' cap; definite though dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes Paragraph 3.b.(1) of the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage, an interaction the provision itself spells out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but self-contained definition; 'any type or form of fungus' is deliberately expansive rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Repeated identically at c149 and c285, so the instrument is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant, including smoke, vapor, soot, fumes' is the classic pollution-definition ambiguity: the general words dwarf the enumerated examples.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same definition appears at c177 and c274 and drives c041, c101 and c117; the copies agree with each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, conventional trade definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in c035, c036 and c063.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical to c005; 'advance written notice' without a stated period is the only softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Untouched by IL 02 61 (c185), which replaces only Paragraph 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 10/30-day notice schedule with no ambiguous term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Replaced for Kansas by IL 02 61 (c185), which adds reasons and a 90-day rule, so two versions sit in one policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A settled last-known-address formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches c007 and the nonrenewal notice rule in c186.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences; the OCR 'will and on that date' does not obscure the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c008 and with the installment cancellation mechanism (c083).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May be less than pro rata' leaves the short-rate basis unstated, a small vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c009; nothing else fixes the refund basis.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One evidentiary sentence; no ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c010 and matches c186.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An integration clause and an amendment-by-endorsement-only rule; each clear, though they pull in opposite directions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy is amended by many endorsements, exactly as this clause allows; duplicates c011.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean audit right with a stated time limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c012 and matches the CGL Premium Audit condition (c255).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any inspections, surveys, reports or recommendations relate only to insurability and the premiums to be charged' is definite; the OCR noise does not change it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states the same condition as c013 in materially different terms (no numbered paragraphs, no boiler and elevator carve-out), leaving two versions in one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two numbered allocations of premium responsibility; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c014 and fits c255.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The printed text says the representative acts 'within the scope of duties as our legal representative' where 'your' is meant, a pronoun slip that inverts the relationship.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c015 prints the same condition correctly, so the two copies differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We will assume you no longer want the insurance' is a deeming provision, and this copy omits the 'and time' element that c016 contains.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It authorises cancellation on a missed installment without expressly observing the 10-day notice in c073 or the Kansas reason-limits in c185.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure applicability sentence naming the layers of conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a fuller statement than the truncated c017 of the same heading, but they are not inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Void' and 'material fact' are settled terms, though materiality is always arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 01 60 (c196) replaces this condition for Kansas with a narrower 'we will not pay' formulation, so the printed avoidance remedy is contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Beyond your direction or control' is a familiar limiter; the location-by-location breach rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.2 (c190) supersedes and rewrites the Control Of Property condition, leaving two versions in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One anti-stacking sentence, definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c020 and pulls against provisions declaring certain coverages 'additional insurance' (c051).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all of the terms' is strict but plain; the two-year period is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 A (c187) replaces this condition with a five-year suit limitation, so the two-year bar printed here is directly contradicted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any revision that would broaden the coverage' is somewhat open, but the operation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c022; nothing else addresses mid-term broadening.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short bailee-exclusion sentence; the OCR gap does not obscure it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c023 and the owner's-account rule in c035c.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The printed condition has an unrelated Special Endorsements heading and premium sentence dropped into the middle of paragraph 2, breaking the sentence that states the excess rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Substantively it matches c024, but the intrusion of the Calculation of Premium text (also printed at c092) makes the boundary between conditions uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This 'provision' is a single OCR block fusing the Calculation of Premium Endorsement with the Other Insurance, Policy Period and Transfer of Rights conditions, so its own scope cannot be read off the page.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its embedded Transfer of Rights text says 'to or from whom' where c026 says 'to or for whom', and its premium sentences duplicate c029; the instrument contains inconsistent copies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise trigger and a closed territory list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c025; the insured premises are in Kansas, well within the territory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To or from whom we make payment' and 'must to nothing after loss' are both errors that alter or garble the obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The other printing of the same condition (c026) says 'to or for whom' and 'must do nothing', and CP 01 01 E (c194) supersedes it for Builders' Risk.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional dividend entitlement, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c030 and fits the other mutual conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed meeting time, date and address; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c031.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short non-assessment guarantee with an OCR spelling slip only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits with the renewal-rating endorsement (c029/c092) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional signpost sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section F of CP 10 30 is in fact printed as Section G (c149-c150), a mismatched cross-reference within the same form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Risks Of Direct Physical Loss' is an all-risk formula whose boundary is set by the exclusions rather than by ambiguous words here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends on Sections B and C of the same form (c100-c133) and on the Declarations showing 'Special', both of which are present.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-concurrent-causation lead-in ('directly or indirectly ... regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence') is one of the most heavily construed sentences in property insurance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the many 'but if ... results in fire we will pay' carve-backs in the same exclusions (c102, c104, c107) and with the ensuing-loss structure of B.2 and B.3.
